prompt.title: Adversarial concurrency and load-test harness generator

var.name: domain_invariants
var.example: stock never negative; successful reservations never exceed initial stock; one reservation per idempotency key

variables.var: what must hold under any interleaving

var.name: runtime
var.example: JDK 25, virtual threads for request handling

variables.var: the JVM and threading model in production

var.name: perf_question
var.example: Does the CAS version keep p99 reserve() under 50 us at 16 threads?

instructions.step: List the shared mutable state and, for each invariant, the interleaving that would break it (thread A reads, thread B reads, A writes, B writes), citing the lines.

For each interleaving, write a race test: N threads wait on a CyclicBarrier, are released together, each performs the operation, and after the round the invariant is asserted; repeat for R rounds and count failing rounds.
Where the window is too narrow to hit reliably, add a test-only seam in the class (a pause hook between read and write, a no-op in production) and use it to widen the window.
Prove each test: run it against the current code and show it fails; then fix the code (atomic compute, CAS loop, lock, or a database constraint) and show it passes the same rounds.

Write JMH benchmarks for {{perf_question}}: @State with the right scope, @Threads at the production concurrency, at least two forks, warmup and measurement iterations, Blackhole for results; report the score with its error.

invariants.inv: Every race test asserts a domain invariant after each round, not merely that no exception was thrown.
Every race test is shown to fail against the unfixed code (a test that cannot fail proves nothing).
Tests synchronize with barriers and latches; Thread.sleep appears only inside the explicit widening seam.
JMH results come from two or more forks with warmup, consume results through Blackhole, and are reported with their error.
On a JDK 21 runtime, no synchronized block guards blocking I/O on virtual threads; the JFR event jdk.VirtualThreadPinned is checked in the load test.

anti_goals.no: No single-run concurrency tests and no tests that pass by luck of scheduling.
No System.nanoTime loops instead of JMH for micro-benchmarks.
No fixing by adding synchronized everywhere; the fix must be the narrowest that restores the invariant, with its throughput measured.

output_contract.file: one race test class per invariant
the fix and the test seam
output_contract.report: For each race test: failing rounds before the fix (out of R) and after; JMH table with score and error per variant.

verification.check: Each race test's assertion names the invariant.
The report shows non-zero failing rounds before the fix for every race test.
grep finds Thread.sleep only in the seam.
The JMH output shows two forks and an error column; the report quotes both.
The load-test JFR recording has no jdk.VirtualThreadPinned events above 20 ms.

prompt.task: Attack the class under test with barrier-released race tests that fail before and pass after your fix, and answer the performance question with JMH.
